EXTRACTION BRAIN NOT INLINED (deviation from unattended-run mechanics 1): mechanics 1 says extraction stays tool-less with its prompt inlined. This run's extraction prompt was 31 KB and the harness truncated it on read, so the coordinator could not produce a byte-exact inline copy or verify one. Rather than hand-transcribe a prompt it could not prove intact - which mechanics 3 explicitly forbids on the split path - extraction was dispatched like the other four seams: Read on its own prompt file, exactly ONE Write to its own answer file, no other tool. The security property is unchanged (the brain still cannot reach outside its prompt); only the delivery mechanism differs. Worth codifying: mechanics 1's 'the prompt fits inline' assumption did not hold this run.

THESIS BRAIN USED EDIT TWICE (disclosed by the subagent, not hidden): the thesis brain's first Write left a stray verdict_note key and one mistyped finding id, and it made two Edit calls on its own answer file to fix both - beyond the Read-plus-one-Write tool rule. The edits touched only its own answer file, reached nothing external, and the deterministic thesis gate then validated the file and passed it on the first attempt, so the gate - not the brain's self-correction - is what admitted the content. Recorded because a brain exceeding its tool wall must never be silent.

CHART-RESEARCH EMPTY-ANSWER SHAPE (coordinator error, logged not hidden): the dispatch told each researcher to write a NO-SERIES-FOUND file when it found nothing. The skill's contract is to leave NO answer file in that case, and CandidateSeries rejects the extra key, so bullet-3's honest empty answer was logged as a validation rejection rather than a clean skip. No data was affected - a bullet with no verified series renders the quiet no-chart line either way - but the rejectedDetail list now carries a schema error that reads like a research failure when it was not one. Fix the dispatch wording next cycle.

GATHERER TOOL-WALL: structural. All three reader-gatherers, the series reader and the three chart researchers were dispatched as the registered web-gatherer subagent type (Read/Write/WebSearch/WebFetch only, no Bash).

BRAIN PROMPT ACCESS + READ-TOOL PAGINATION (accepted practice, F128): judge (3 samples), thesis, implication and narrator ran on model opus with Read on their own pre-split prompt files and one Write to their own answer file. Each emitted prompt was split into <seam>-system.txt, <seam>-schema.json and numbered ~30 KB <seam>-user-partN.txt chunks by work/daily-2026-08-24/split_prompt.py, which ASSERTS the rejoined chunks reproduce the original user string byte-for-byte before any dispatch. All four rejoins verified exact (judge 143776 B / 5 parts, thesis 168412 B / 6, implication 146026 B / 5, narrator 302728 B / 11). No prompt text was altered - only how it is stored on disk.
